title: Low Estrogen, High Prolactin Levels - Seeking Advices
selftext:
Hello everyone,

I'm a 45-year-old man dealing with some challenging symptoms that have recently surfaced, such as sudden, unexplained anxiety and fear—emotions that are quite unusual for me. Previously, I was diagnosed with PTSD, but after years of successful therapy, I had been symptom-free.

I've been on venlafaxine and pregabalin for about 20 years without any issues. However, due to the recent emotional changes, my psychiatrist prescribed duloxetine to address these issues, but unfortunately, my symptoms worsened.

I decided to have my blood tested, and the results showed low estrogen, high prolactin, while my testosterone levels are normal. Additionally, my cholesterol levels are also high.

Has anyone here experienced something similar? I'm trying to understand what could be causing these hormonal imbalances and how to manage them. Any insights or advice would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you in advance for your help.

title: Trying to find the best medication to treat Generalized Anxiety Disorder and PTSD without worsening sexual dysfunction or causing weight gain
selftext:
Very specific question incoming.  Wanted to get a preliminary idea of what the options really are before we go make a psych appointment.  I am a medical student at a MD school in the southern US using a throwaway account to ask this question on behalf of my wife.  I have tried to find answers to this everywhere; my textbooks, UpToDate, Dynamed, Wikipedia, etc.  I do know some psychiatrists from my psych clerkship but don't really want to ask this question in person to them due to the personal nature of this situation.  The history is below for some context, but basically she is in therapy and doing well, and I believe that medication would help a great deal but we haven't been to a psychiatrist yet.  We want to find the best medication that would treat Generalized Anxiety Disorder (first and foremost), as well as PTSD, without making her sexual dysfunction worse than it is now.  I'm aware that GAD and PTSD are generally treated with SSRIs or SNRIs, but these medications are notorious for their sexual side effect profile.  Additionally, I know that Bupropion is the antidepressant with the least sexual side effects that you would move to next after SSRIs for most of the disorders that SSRIs treat, but it appears that there is no evidence of Bupropion being an effective treatment for GAD; other non-sexual side effect antidepressant drugs like Vortioxetine or Vilazodone have a similar story.  I'm aware that Mirtazapine can be used to treat GAD and doesn't really cause sexual side effects, but my wife has been trying very hard to lose weight recently by exercising frequently (180 lbs mostly adipose tissue to 170 lbs mostly lean body mass in the last year, yay!) and does not want to take something that is know to commonly cause weight gain (like Mirtazapine.)  So what would be a good option for her?  Is there another drug that I'm unaware of that would treat GAD, PTSD, and not worsen sexual side effects or cause weight gain?  Or should she try an SSRI/SNRI and see if it affects her sex drive?  Or should she try Mirtazapine and see if it affects her weight?  

History: My wife (25yo F) has had Generalized Anxiety Disorder for her entire life that was diagnosed a couple years ago.  Additionally, she has PTSD from an episode of sexual assault at age 18.  She has been seeing a therapist for these issues approximately twice a month for a little less that one year.  Due to both of these conditions and the nature of her assault she has been dealing with significant anxiety around anything to do with sexuality, and is specifically avoidant of penises (all penises, not just my own, before anybody decides to make jokes) as they are somewhat of a "trigger" for her anxiety.  Basically the only time that we are ever intimate is after we have both been drinking (don't worry, we've discussed consent at great length while sober and both agreed that we're fine with everything in the bedroom after some drinks and we know our boundaries, etc.), because it is the only time that she can overcome her anxiety about intimacy.  99% of the time, our intimacy is me pleasuring her and then her apologizing that she is not able to do the same to me, which I am perfectly ok with as I know that it will take a significant amount of time and therapy for this issue to be resolved.  She is in therapy, 2x per month for a year, mainly CBT and EMDR.  Has not tried any medication so far.

Age: 25

Sex: F

Height: 5'7"

Weight: 170 lbs 

Race: Caucasian, non-Hispanic

Duration of complaint: 7 years

Location: Southern USA

Any existing relevant medical issues: GAD, PTSD

Current medications: combined oral contraceptives

title: Something's DEFINITELY Wrong with my Brain. (Trans [FtM], 16)
selftext:
I can't think straight, it's hard to keep a consistent train of thought, I forget things WAY too much (like, I forget what I'm talking about 1/3 of the time, same goes for when I go to do something. Sometimes I remember, other times I don't.) my head is constantly cloudy, I am physically incapable of performing complex math anymore, I live my life mostly unaware of anyone's problems (even my own), I am starting to feel like I'm losing the ability to function properly, I get headaches, and there's definitely more that I can't manage to pull out of my brain.

Oh, and I'm 16. this started a couple of years ago, and has been getting exponentially worse.

I have:

ADHD

A Depressive Disorder

Borderline Personality Disorder

A major Anxiety Disorder

Autism

(Undiagnosed) DID

(Undiagnosed) PTSD

And I take medication for the Anxiety, ADHD, and Depression. People keep saying that it's probably how my meds interact, and they want me to write down whenever I feel like this but I can't because I ALWAYS do and it makes it hard to describe most of the time! I just want them to scan my brain, just in case, but my mom keeps saying we have to wait for a referral to a Neurologist but I didn't even get to talk to my normal doctor! They had me talk to her nurse! And they just say it's my meds, but this started back before I even started most of these meds! I feel like it can't be my meds, it feels like it just can't be that simple.

title: Reddit, should I be concerned?
selftext:
I know damn well that a lot of people - especially teenagers my age - tend to question their health, rely on diagnoses, and overthink, but I'd appreciate some feedback. I know it's long, but please please please help if you can. 

( If you don't want to read it, at least click on the link and listen to the video of my mouth. It'll freak you out. Luv u ♥️ )

I'm a 16 year old female. I'm 5'5 and weigh about 105 pounds. I'm half Filipino(mom) and half American(dad). My mom is of latino descent. I usually take 60mg of Dextroamphetamine(Adderall XR) in the morning, 1mg of Prazosin(Minipress) at night, birth control, and Sertraline(Zoloft). I'm not sure if this is relevant, but heart, lung, sleep, and brain problems are very common in both sides of my family. My dad actually had a brain tumor that hemorrhaged, which is cool. (Dad, if you see this, hi! Get off Reddit and hug me, damn it.)

Anyways, my main concerns are my excessive sleepiness and shortness of breath. Now, I know what you're probably thinking. 

A teenager? Tired? How UNIQUE and CONCERNING! 

It's a bit more than that, though. I'm SO TIRED. 
But this is fairly recent. And it's getting worse. I just kinda want some tips and coping mechanisms with my excessive sleepiness, though, so if you don't care about that please skip to my shortness of breath paragraph. I just hope that my tiredness isn't related to my heart or lungs or anything.


Short backstory: Last September, I underwent a very traumatic event and was raped. The trauma really didn't end there, though. It dragged on until June 2018 due to  constant harassment and threats. From September - December 2017, i rarely slept. I'm talking about a ridiculously small amount of sleep - around 2 hours worth every 3 or 4 days. During this period of temporary insomnia, I was having intense hallucinations and was going to counseling for my PTSD. At some point, though, my body had had enough sleep deprivation, and I was unable to stay awake for ANYTHING. I was then prescribed Prazosin, Sertraline, and Adderall. I was thought to potentially have narcolepsy, since it runs in my dad's family. Since then, I've struggled with extreme fatigue and tiredness.

Today I recieved my sleep study and polysomnogram results, which were not consistent with narcolepsy. I DO have an incredibly fast sleep onset, though, and can sleep within 2 minutes. This was relieving but has me wondering if my excessive sleepiness is trauma induced. Can anyone conclude this? Besides managing a sleep schedule, how do I combat my sleepiness? Is this normal? I've fallen asleep driving(while stopped in traffic), in every class hour almost every day, while talking, eating, typing, walking, etc. I have constant sleepwalking and talking episodes, but my PSG showed no REM abnormalities. My dad wants to lower my adderall dosage, but I'm barely managing on 60mg. I don't know how to begin to convey my tiredness. I have cataplexy-like episodes of muscle weakness and fatigue when stressed or physically exerted, and fall asleep almost immediately after. Ultimately I'm mainly concerned about my grades, safety, and presentation since I'm always drowsy. I just want to cope and not have it interfere with my daily life. I usually sleep at about 10:30pm and wake up at 7, but I'm often exhausted and sleep even earlier. :( However, I nap a lot during the day and try to avoid napping past 4. It's probably just how I deal with stress, but the sleepiness itself stresses me out even more. What else can I even do? At least if I had narcolepsy I'd have solid answers. The best advice they had for me was to correct my sleeping schedule, but I shit you not I've slept for days and still felt uncontrollably tired.  It's very frustrating to sleep through things I don't want to miss. It's very frustrating to know I can dismiss puzzle alarms in my sleep. It's frustrating to know that when I sleep talk I say things I don't mean. My dad punched a hole in my door because I was conversing with him while asleep, lmao. I don't even know what I want anymore. 


NOW FOR MY NEXT AND MORE IMPORTANT CONCERN! 

 It's actually more important than the sleepiness, so sorry for the long paragraphs. 

Short backstory: When I was 8, I used an inhaler as needed because i lived in SLC and the smog was terrible. I didn't use it much at all though. 

I moved to a different place in Utah without smog in January 2017 and completely forgot about my inhaler.

 However, since about March I've become increasingly fatigued and out of breath. It's gotten really bad lately and I was prescribed my inhaler again. It doesn't help much. At all. My peak flow chart does increase, though... My doctor doesn't know if it's asthma or not.

I wouldn't be too concerned except I've also developed an externally audible heartbeat in my mouth. I can't stand up or roll over without wheezing, and my heartbeat is very fast. My muscles become weak and I almost collapse if I don't catch my breath. It is audible when my mouth is closed, but it is a lot louder when my mouth is open. In a silent room, you can hear it from about 5 feet away. This happens with any exertion, all day, every day. The heartbeat thing started in June or July. Since then, my muscle weakness and shortness of breath have been worse than ever. 

Here is a video of my heartbeat!
 https://photos.app.goo.gl/qFaxrHAhWpNZXwxf7 

Ignore my disgusting mouth. I have other recordings, but this one's the clearest and it's easiest to see that it's in conjunction with my heart. 

This also interferes with my daily life. It sucks! I've had an EKG done a few months ago with no major concerns, and my lungs sound normal on a stethoscope. 

My adderall makes it a bit worse, but my heartbeat thing, weakness, and shortness of breath happens even without it. Same with the Prazosin and sertraline and birth control. I can't walk to one class to another without being late because I constantly have to catch my breath. :( I don't know how to combat this either. Is it something I should be concerned about? Because I'm kinda concerned. I just don't know what to do about it, since my inhaler doesn't help me much. Anyone have an explanation to what the hell the sound is? My lungs? My heart? It's probably nothing, but that coupled with muscle weakness, chest pain, and fatigue is enough to convince me it might be something else.  

What do y'all think? Should I be doing anything to treat this? Does anyone know what it is? Is it normal? Should I be watching out for anything? I don't know, I'm probably paranoid. It's just weird. And uncomfortable. I hate being so aware of my heart.

 I like freaking people out with my mouth, but at the end of the day, it freaks me out the most. I dunno. Any feedback would be cool, even if it's just "wtf ur heart sounds like 2 dudes banging." 

this probably didn't make much sense because i was half asleep writing some of this but yeah

TL,DR;
im very very very tired and dont know how to deal with it, and ive ruled out narcolepsy. i think it's trauma induced. i also am very weak and cant breathe a lot. and i hear my heart in my mouth and it is very loud

title: Diagnosed with ADHD-PI and have a daily prescription for Adderall IR. The medication is life-changing for me, but I'm worried about long-term side effects. Would love some resources/thoughts from qualified doctors.
selftext:
Hi all,   


I am a 23-year-old woman diagnosed with moderate to severe ADHD, primarily inattentive (severity depending primarily on the symptoms, as I could manage some better than others). Medication has been genuinely life-changing for me, by either eliminating or minimizing all symptoms, including a tendency toward rumination and dysphoric existential feelings that stemmed from severe and frequent under-stimulation.  


However, I've heard a lot of talk about stimulants (and Adderall in particular) being either directly bad for you or dangerous over time. This is the only medication I will have ever been on regularly and in an ongoing, potentially lifelong way. My fear about the effects of the medicine has me feeling unsafe and unsure. I've considered trying a different medicine that has less concern surrounding it, but I'm reluctant to try something else when this has worked so well for me.  


Specific details, regimen, and health history: As far as I'm aware, I do not have a heart condition, abnormal blood pressure, a history of addiction, or anything that should theoretically put me at risk for issues with this treatment (in myself or in my family in general). My provider has me prescribed with 20mg of Adderall IR 2x a day, and then one 10mg of Adderall IR in the late evening. So, essentially, one 20mg tablet when I wake up, one 20mg tablet 4-5 hours later, and then one 10mg tablet 4-5 hours after that. Over the course of a 15-ish hour day, I am taking a total of 50mg Adderall IR daily, with days off. As far as I'm aware, the dose isn't based on height or weight, but I'll include that in case it does matter: 5'2", 110-120lbs (not sure of exact weight as I haven't been weighed in a while). I was originally on 15mg 2x a day, but we found that my symptoms were pervasive for the last half of the day, and many of my symptoms involve emotional difficulty and trouble with relaxing, so we added the booster to enable full-day coverage. We also bumped up the 15mg tablets to 20mg tablets a couple of weeks ago for the titration process to see if there were additional benefits and if the side-effects were still tolerable. If relevant, I'm unsure if I've noticed an increase in benefits of the 20s, but I have noticed an increase in mild side-effects such as nausea/mild anxiety if I take it on an empty stomach in the morning.

title: What could be the cause of someone just suddenly losing their ability to form a coherent sentence?
selftext:
I work at an independent living facility. A resident here (74M) one day came up to the desk and was just suddenly completely unable to form a rational sentence. He can say words but stringed together they don't make any sense. 

This came out of absolutely nowhere. I spoke with him frequently before this. Sometimes for hours on end and he was consistently witty and is highly intelligent. He was a computer programmer before he retired. He was very good with wordplay and so for this to happen out of the blue was shocking.

He was taken to the hospital and they ruled out every common cause. Every scan and test revealed no sign of a stroke. No signs of brain damage. No heart damage. They're sending him back here as is because they can't figure out what's wrong and he's still completely coherent and able to understand everything people are saying. 

It's like he's exactly the same but just... forgot how to talk and form sentences. And no one at that hospital can figure out how or why.

I care about this man a lot so I was wondering if anyone here might have even the faintest idea? I will say, I highly suspect he's on the autism spectrum. He has very poor social understand of cues and poor hygiene. Due to the generation he's from though with very little awareness, he would never seek a diagnosis. I can't confirm it or course, nor can I link it to whatever has happened to him. But it's the only idea I have.

Any ideas?

title: Adderall "calm": myth or undiagnosed adhd?
selftext:
Demographic info: 22F, asian, 5'3" and 50kg, current meds are 60mg fluoxetine, long psychiatric history. I drink, smoke, and use recreational drugs. 

I took 20 mg Adderall XR yesterday for the first time in my life when offered by a close friend with diagnosed ADHD. make you (it was a Friday and I was all caught up for the week anyways). I did a regular amount of work in a day but it was less anxiety inducing than usual I suppose. It was like time and my brain slowed down. 

Now, I tried to do some googling and there are some people who claim it's an urban myth that becoming calm on adderall = undiagnosed adhd. So, is it? 
I'm hesitant to ask either my doctor or my counselor because I don't want to be labeled as a "substance user" on my psych records

title: I had a bilateral salpingectomy and have taken five positive pregnancy tests. How? Did my doctor mess up? Forget to do it and altered the chart after? So scared and confused.
selftext:
I had a bilateral salpingectomy and have taken five positive pregnancy tests. Did my doctor mess up? Forget to do it and altered the chart? I am so confused.

F32 5'3' 130lbs
Medications: celexa (anxiety), Adderall (ADHD), potassium citrate (kidney stones)

My baby is 17 months and it was a very traumatic birth. I had cesarean scheduled at 39 weeks, but she decided to come earlier than that at 38 weeks. Unfortunately, that meant the on call doctor was going to deliver her. From several past bad experiences I didn't have confidence in her ability as a doctor, but baby is coming, so not really up to me. She complained to the nurse that she had to come in after dinner for me so I already had the impression her headspace was not where it needed to be. 

She didn't look at my chart, or not closely to see that I had an anterior placenta. I hemorrhaged and they couldn't get her out for what felt like forever. I see a ton of people rushing in and when she's out she's not breathing and everyone is working on her. The doctor is doing all the rest of the stuff and when the sheet is moved her and the nurse's face are absolutely covered in blood. She was frazzled and very nervous. My baby comes around and by the 5 minute APGAR is at 9 instead of 1 and didn't even need to be in the NICU. I am so thankful and it was the scariest time of my life.

But my question is: could she have botched my bilateral salpingectomy? Could she have maybe forgotten to even do it? I know that doctors are used to high stress and what is scary to me may not be to them, but this person was obviously not ok. She was shaking and pale and very nervous when the curtain came down and I was stitched up. Or did she not see that I was to have a bi salp after delivery? If she looked at my chart, it wasn't very closely. I did mention it in the beginning to her, but with the scary event and the fact that she didn't seem very interested in what I had to say, I'm wondering if it was even done or done accurately. How could this happen? Can anyone offer insight into this? 

I did look up her reports to verify if it was done. They are not detailed at all. Doesn't mention a salpingectomy at all, glosses over the blood loss and even though it was more than 1800 she said it was "no more than expected" in her report. Didn't say anything about my baby not breathing or any mention of the placenta whatsoever. For being in there for 90 minutes, it was very, very short. 

Labs mention the fallopian tubes, but no detail besides the exact same descriptors for each, like they could have been copied and pasted identically. I am freaking out. I don't understand and I need to hear from professionals any likely scenario. I am NOT going back to that doctor. She will never treat me again.

title: For my Brother, Neurologist's staff dropped the ball. Now how do I complain to the Doctor, and help my Brother get care in a different state?
selftext:
tl;dr: I took my brother to my awesome neurologist. His staff dropped the ball big-time. How do I raise it with my Neurologist and get my brother the care he needs? 


Neurologist's State: Virginia

Brother's State: Massachusetts (just ended the EO that allowed him to do telehealth visits with the Virginian Neurologist)

My Brother's Age: 40

Gender: Male

Weight: about 200 lbs

Location: Head

Duration: Years

Medical History: Migraines/Headaches, ADHD, PTSD

Current Meds: Vyvanse for ADHD, and trying to figure out the rest

Health Insurance: Obamacare plan - Tufts Health Together


**BACKGROUND:**  My Brother was getting sub-standard care from Neurology Nurse Practitioners in Boston for his mental health and headaches/migraines. (For example, first NP would give him ADHD meds, then would leave the practice, and the new one would abruptly cut him off, and switch him to anti-depression meds).  I had him come to Virginia to see my General Neurologist.  


**TIMELINE:** My Neurologist evaluated my brother, and gave him an overview of what he thinks it's going on, as well as a plan moving forward by trying different meds.  My Neurologist was drafting a report and was supposed to send it to my brother on Sept 1, and never did.  On Sept 13, the Neurologist was supposed to send over a prescription for medicine X, and never did.  On Sept 15, the state of Mass EO ended, so my Neurologist could not see my brother remotely.  His office stopped responding completely to him.  **There was no continuity of care.**  


**NOW WHAT?** My brother is upset - he's been left hanging, and paid a few thousand dollars for these appts (out of pocket).  I'm going to see the Neurologist next week. I need to keep him as my Neurologist, but I also want him to make it up to my brother. **What do I say, what I ask for, and HOW do I say it?**


Thanks.


PS. In Boston, there are lots of Neurologists, but his plan doesn't have very many.  He often sees Neurology Nurse Practitioners, who aren't familiar with ADHD. Instead of keep looking, I thought it'd be faster for him to see a good one in Virginia.

title: Bad anesthesia/pain medicine reaction, possible allergy?
selftext:
This is going to be long, but I feel like context is important here. 

Yesterday I (34F, white) had a laparoscopic bilateral salpingectomy to lower my risk of ovarian cancer (family history) and because we have 3 kids and want permanent birth control. I have had three previous outpatient surgeries (nasal septoplasty/turbinate reduction, ureteroscopic kidney stone removal, shoulder arthroscopy). Those all went pretty darn well, except for a lot of post op nausea. But I was still really nervous going in for this procedure. They gave me a scopolamine patch about an hour before the procedure. I was wheeled back and my team took great care of me and the whole thing went great. Until I got to PACU. When I woke up, I felt different than in my other three recoveries. I could not hold my head in midline if my life depended on it. I could not make my mouth make words, even though I could think in relatively normal sentences. I could not move my body though. It was so strange. Controlling my limbs was extremely difficult. I felt like I had zero muscle tone. I was in some pain for the procedure so they gave me three doses of IV fentanyl in the PACU, I think the total was around 120 mcg. Then they moved me back into stage two recovery or whatever, where my husband was waiting in my room. By this time I felt high AF. The only medication I regularly take is methylphenidate for diagnosed ADHD and probably too much Advil because I have three little kids. So it seems like that was a lot of fentanyl. And apparently they did a full intubation which was different than my other surgeries, which just used the laryngeal mask thing. So I had rocuronium and a reversal agent in the OR. So moving into stage 2 recovery was when things really started to get weird for me. I still felt totally flaccid and couldn’t move my legs and had to conjure up extreme mental focus to even push the call light or swallow sips of water. And at one point I had full on hives all over my trunk and up to my neck that came on pretty quickly and only lasted 15-30 minutes before disappearing again. A lot of all of this is a big blur, but my husband (who is extremely caring and supportive to the point that one of the nurses even commented on it) was starting to get really concerned - I felt like I was pretty mentally coherent the whole time but my husband says I was pretty out of it. And I remember one of the experienced and awesome nurses saying something that he felt like I had looked somewhat seizure-y for a moment. I also was having some issues with urinary retention. I tried 3 or 4 times in a bed pan and a commode to empty my bladder but I just could not get the flow started. They did a bladder scan and were just about ready to do a straight catheter when I tried one more time and was able to go, but it was still very difficult and took a lot of concentration to make anything happen. The on call doctor came in at some point, by which time the hives were gone, and she suggested taking off the scopolamine patch and seeing if that helped. I think it did, along with giving the fentanyl time to wear off. But from the time I was out of surgery to the time they let me go home, it was more than 5 hours. I’m coming up on 24 hours post op and I just now can stand up without feeling like I’m going to collapse. 

So my questions are 1) could that all be attributed to scopolamine and too much fentanyl? 2) Is it possible that some of it was the lingering effects of the rocuronium? 3) what could have caused transient hives like that? 4) should I be concerned about any of this? I know at some point I’ll have to have another surgery for my shoulder again and possibly another kidney stone removal. What do I tell my future provider, other than it was the worst/only trip of my life?

115lbs

5’4”

United States

title: Strange blood results but the ER doc claimed they were fine (I saw them the next day)
selftext:

Diagnoses: hEDS, fibromyalgia, PTSD, MDD, chronic migraine, dysautonomia, CVST (2020) (still working on testing for blood disorders but negative for everything except Lupus Anticoagulant, though negative on every lupus test I've done)

  ***

***

title: Guidance regarding 12 y/o
selftext:
Good evening, friends. My bride and I adopted 2 young men in June.  The oldest (age 12, 5’2”, 117 lbs), who unfortunately endured more hardships than any ever should, has become a bit of an onion; once we peel one layer off, something else is uncovered.  

Thus far, we’ve been diagnosed with anxiety, ADHD, and PTSD.  He also sees a counselor weekly (who he adores).  As of late, the greatest concern revolves around sleep.  He often comments that he never sleeps, but I truly wrote it off to pre-teens feeling exhausted.  Over the last 10 days, he finds himself in an unwakeable sleep.  The only comparison I can make is when my friends and I would come home from the bar and one would pass out.  I have to “fireman carry” him to his bedroom.

He’s also begun to twitch (either L or R leg, always R arm).  In some events, he will call me, or my wife, and asks for nobody to hurt him; therefore, my mind went to night terrors.  Contradictory to the previous scenario, he also has times that there is only twitching.

There are also times he awakes in what seems to be utter confusion taking approximately 20 minutes to find his footing. Questions include, “Where am I?” “Who are you?” “Are we going somewhere?”

I can’t help but wonder if the twitching could be seizure related.  For all I know, it could be a kin to puberty.

With all this in mind, I’m an educator and not a physician.  I’ve contacted our pediatrician and am anticipating a referral to our regional children’s hospital.  Any guidance from my fellow Redditor’s would be greatly appreciated.

Is this something I should go to the doctor with? My period has never lasted this long before but doesn’t everyone experience this at some point?

title: I'm suspecting that I might be on the autism spectrum. How likely is it? Is it even worth looking into?
selftext:
I am 22, female. I don't drink nor smoke, I have asthma (but I didn't have many problems with it lately) and anemia. I am from Romania. Don't know if that matters to the topic at hand, but I'm putting it here.

I'm beginning to suspect I might be on the autism spectrum.

English is not my first language, sorry if I make mistakes.

So I barely have anyone to talk to in my life, let alone about this. I hope this is a good place to post this. It's kinda hard for me to put my thoughts into words, but I'll try to keep it as short and organized as possible and I'll try not to ramble too much.

Lately I've started to realize slowly that there's something off with me. Or rather, some things. I didn't pay much attention to it, because separately and not giving it much thought it seems normal, if not a bit weird, but nothing that bad. However, an event at work recently prompted me to start thinking about it much more and I've realized there's many things about me that might be associated with the spectrum, but I don't know if I'm just looking for excuses or attention or whatever (even if I am super secretive about it, I don't know, my brain just thinks that way).

I should probably mention that no one in my family has autism, but nor did they get a diagnosis. Or if they did, they never told me. My mom struggled with anxiety and depression (not claiming diagnosis, just by the way she was), my father has really bad anger issues. So there's no history, or I don't know about it.

I'll try to organize it because I know how tough for me at least it is to see a whole block of text scattered around with the main points hard to find.

# 1. FACIAL EXPRESSION AND EXPRESSING MYSELF:

***1-1.*** I'm starting with this because this is that recent thing I talked about. Recently, at work, a coworker mentioned how I always look "sad". Granted, I'm not the happiest, but usually it's just a middle ground. My immediate explanation to her was "I am just a bit expressionless" (something along the lines). It was normal. I was like yeah, that's pretty much it. But then I thought: Wait, that's odd actually, isn't it? So that started me thinking about more and more details about me...

***1-2.*** I find it really hard to put my thoughts into words. Even this whole post is hard for me to express. In my head I could have all of these things put together: I would know how to put it, what to put, etc. But when it comes down to it... It just... It isn't there. I don't know what happens.

***1-3.*** I mentioned above that I'm kinda expressionless and I'm almost always not feeling much (unless it's about certain things). I just push a lot away, I find. If someone actually tries to crack me open, I find it hard not to cry. It's hard to talk about my life, because I feel like I failed at life. I'm not sure if this has to do with anything, but I thought I'd mention it while I'm at it.

# 2. SPEECH AND COMMUNICATION:

***2-1.*** I'm basically quiet and introverted and often shy. I try to avoid getting attention as much as possible. I could be dying and I still would want not to be noticed.

***2-2.*** When communicating, I'm often more the listener. I do not know how to start conversations nor how to hold them. I barely know what to say in response to what people are telling me and it just becomes awkward, especially if they do expect a reply and I'm just struggling over there to find an appropriate reply.

***2-3.*** I work in retail and I have for a while, yet after all this time, I still don't know what I am supposed to say, or if I'm even supposed to say anything at all. I thought that practice makes perfect, but it just doesn't. Don't get me wrong, I am capable of communicating, but it's very, VERY choppy and awkward, or that's how I feel it is anyway. Mostly I notice the way other coworkers talk among themselves and I try to copy that to the best of my abilities, but it's still weird.

***2-4.*** I feel like everything that comes out of my mouth is weird, misplaced or... just not like it should be. I don't know how to explain this phenomenon. It's like I could be saying the exact same thing someone else says, but it would sound way better if they say it.

On top of all, I don't have much in common since I have very limited interests (will come to that in a bit).

***2-5.*** When I talk to people, I find it uncomfortable to look them in the eyes. When I'm more used to someone, I can kinda pull it off, but otherwise it's just... not. If I try to make eye contact, I find that I stare too much, too intensely.

***2-6.*** Sometimes I try to say something, but nothing comes out. My mouth is moving (under my mask thankfully, so people don't see me just mouthing nothing) but it won't come out.

***2-7.*** I also have this thing where at random points in time I would remember/think about something, be it a situation that happened, a conversation, something I watched, etc and I would repeat part of it (a word, phrase, depends).

***2-8.*** I tend to come across very cold, but sometimes, with certain people, I get really clingy. Annoyingly clingy. I hate it.

***2-9.*** I find it easier to gesture towards something or just explain things in any way that doesn't include me talking. Of course, I can't do that for everything, but if I can... Why not?

# 3. TICS... STIMS?

So I have a bunch of tics, or stims, or whatever they're called. Please take into consideration that I'm not saying this is stims or a sign of autism necessarily, I don't know if all of this is normal or not, I'm just adding this to my case. Most of these I've been doing without thinking of it, only lately have I started to pick up on them.

The one I had for the longest time is bouncing my legs. I bounce my legs so much that back in highschool my classmate would tell me to stop, I was bouncing the desk with me. I also kick my feet against the chair, although less frequent. I also tend to spin on a chair if it has wheels.

Another thing I do is bite my nails. Everyday, for as long as I can remember. I do it so bad that sometimes my nails end up a mess that looks like someone took a hammer too. I've got questions of "What happened to your nails?" and it's always awkward to try and answer, I just try to brush it off if I can.

I pick at my dead skin. If I had a wound, small or not, I pick at it. Could bleed, but I'll still do it again. I don't know. It's addicting.

I snap my fingers. Like, I pull them backwards and crackle (I hope that's the word) them. Again, I do this a lot as well.

I sway from side to side, especially in my chair.

If I have a shirt that's close to my neck, I pull it down. Constantly. It's annoying, but I just can't help myself.

I rub my eyes. So. much. It's the reason why I almost never wear makeup. (Well, I'm bad at it too, but rubbing my eyes is definitely the main reason)

When I'm very excited I shake my legs (like full on kick them) and shake my arms/hands. Although, only my interest can get me this excited.

When I feel overwhelmed (especially at work), I have the big urge to scratch my forehead (or scratch in general) or hit something, or throw something. Of course, I don't, because that would be kinda weird to explain to my supervisors, but I really wanna do it. When I'm left alone I don't hold back that much though. I'm ashamed to say that my other laptop broke down because of me. Granted, it was not the greatest, most functional laptop to begin with, but still, I'm at least part of the cause.

This one's not as frequent, but sometimes when I'm laying in bed I would start swaying, almost like I'm trying to roll myself in flour.

This one is very rare and situational, but there's times when I just spin in circles.

# 4. RELATING TO OTHERS:

***4-1.*** I'll just straight up say it. I'm not the most empathetic person. I know it's a quality everyone should have, but I just can't put myself into someone else's shoes most of the time. I can't. Yes, I can rationalize it based on past experience, something like: "I've been through this so I know how it is, however I can not feel it at this moment".

***4-2.*** I also apparently can't figure out people's thoughts, emotions and stuff. While I do go along with the conversation to the best of my abilities, I don't know if it's good or bad. I also can't decipher emotions very well. The most recent example is when a coworker got mad because I "didn't do anything" about what was happening. I tried to tell her that I had no clue what happened (especially since we were kinda separated. I could see her, but I wouldn't be able to tell what was the problem), and she mentioned I could've seen that she was agitated.

I honestly didn't realize she was. Now I don't know if this is me having poor understanding of people's behaviour or if she really was off with her behaviour, but I just thought it's worth mentioning. If I did realize it, I would've tried to know what was going on, of course I would have, but I just didn't notice. It wasn't intentional.

# 5. SPECIAL INTEREST:

Boy, oh boy. This one's a big one. I mean BIG. I was literally obsessed with one manga for about a decade (no, I'm not exagerating). Obsessed. I would keep up with anything new, I would always try to find something about it, I would have hundreds of thousands of photos, videos, my life revolved around it. It was so bad that I had a hard time finding anything new with it. I usually try to keep it to myself, because I know it'd be annoying, but when I'm permitted I could talk about it for days. Yeah, sure, not nonstop because that would be humanly impossible, but I hope you get what I mean.

Now, I have a different special interest. It is a show. A very popular and ongoing show. It started smoothly. Then it evolved into me searching every little thing about it, it's characters, it's lore, etc. I started hoarding photos, videos, keeping up with the new things. Basically everything I did with the other one. I am obsessed. Recently I talked to someone for days about it. It didn't even matter if she wasn't that knowledgeable (as I said, it's a popular show so she knew it, but she wasn't actively watching it). Oh, god, I can talk day in, day out about it, I will NOT get tired.

One friend mentioned how I find so many videos with it.

Yeah. That's because I scratch every corner of Youtube's butt about it. I am actively searching and hoarding. I'd buy anything that relates even a bit to it, even if just thematically (so it doesn't matter necessarily if it's specially made for the show -although I would love it-, it just has to be related in some way). I spent my money on dumb stuff that I could have gone without, just because it reminded me of it.

Now granted, I do have other things I like. I like gaming for example. I also write once in a while. But I can go days without it. Without my special interest, however, I cannot. This is something I think about everyday, every night before sleep even.

# 6. LIFESTYLE/ROUTINE AND ROLE IN SOCIETY:

***6-1.*** So... I have a routine. Not a great one, really, but a routine. I don't like it being disturbed. I don't like sudden changes, I don't like spontaneous decisions. Please, if you decide something, at least tell me... A week in advance at most. I try to get over it though if my brother (caretaker) sets something, because I guess I owe it to him and also he would just start arguing and say I don't want to do anything and just... I don't want to argue. I don't want to fight. There's many things about me and my brother, but I won't get much into it because it doesn't have to do with the topic at hand. But let me tell you, I hate it.

***6-2.*** I failed college. It was my biggest failure of my life. Especially because it was so preventable. Thing is, ever since middle school I started getting progressively more shy and in highschool I was just... not there. I mean, I was in the class, but it never felt like I belonged. I only made a friend that I still have to this day, but only because she stuck around despite my nature.

In highschool, I thought college will be my moment. The moment I break out of my shell and become who I've never been. Oh, I didn't expect it to turn around this way. I didn't make any friends at all, I barely talked to anyone. At one point I started becoming overwhelmed, but I don't know by what. I started going to parks and such instead of going to college, all in secrecy. I became ashamed to show my face after this, I know I should have, but instead I just continued this. Missed more and more classes, of course failed my exams. Actually, didn't even show up for most.

Well, I dropped out and got into another one, same subject. History repeats again. I'm ashamed.

You see, I've never failed a class before, so this was way more than academic failure. I blew up two chances at college, both in good universities with a subject I really liked and was good at (foreign languages). This is my biggest regret in life, but I can't turn back now. So I got a job. I'm not really well, it kinda overwhelms me (ironically even when there's not much to do), but hey... I guess at least I make money being miserable now. I try to get any piece of what I missed through the occasional foreign clients whom I can use my english with.

6-3. I feel like an alien. I know it sounds weird, but that's the best way I can put it. I feel like I've come from another place, put on a disguise and I'm walking around trying to convince people that I'm one of them. After so much time, I still don't feel like I belong. It feels like I never belong anywhere. I feel like I'm faking everything. I'm like an alien visiting Earth.

# 7. SMALL THINGS I DON'T KNOW HOW TO CATEGORISE:

***7-1.*** I don't remember much of when I was little, but I know that when I got upset, oh, I got upset. I would scream and yell and I would be a pain. My family still brings it up. It disappoints me, because I'm an adult and now, while yes I still get overwhelmed, I always try to avoid arguing and try to be as calm as possible. I'm an adult, I'm not that little girl anymore and it's not fair to make it as if it's a valid argument for anything ("Oh remember you were acting like a child when you were a child?" basically). Anyway, that's not the point, the point is I was very loud. I don't know if that's relevant, but hey.

***7-2.*** Even my mom (who's not with us on the earth anymore sadly) considered the possibility of autism. However, it never went further. It was just a passing thing.

\---

Now that that's over (and hopefully not missing too much), there's just some things that are on my mind along with this. How do I even begin? I don't know if it's the same like with a physical doctor, or what. I can't tell my brother because he'd just laugh me off and not take me seriously. At worst, he'd start saying it's because of this and that and make it a big argument. But I have no clue where to begin, or who even occupies with diagnoses. Psychiatrists? Or is it psychologists? I don't know.

Besides that, I have many doubts... What if I am wrong? What if I'm just looking for excuses? What if I'm subconsciously like "I'm so bad at life I must pick at anything to shift blame". I mean, in a way, it would feel comforting to know that there is a reason for all of this. It would not immediately solve my problems, but I wouldn't feel so bad about my experiences. But maybe I'm just picking apart something that isn't there?

I know it's a spectrum, but what if I'm still not quite there? Maybe I'm imagining things? Like, are my stims not specific enough or maybe they're normal things everyone does? Is it still a special interest if it changed? Is my special interest too normal to be considered a special interest in that way?

Maybe I'm just socially inept. Maybe... I don't know. Maybe I'm just whiny. Maybe I feel overwhelmed at work (and academically before) because I'm just bad and I should get a hold of myself. I don't know. Is it really a stretch to think I might be on the spectrum?

And if I decide at one point to pursue a diagnosis (when I have the money and I know what I'm doing) would it even be worth it? I'm just kinda lost about it all. I guess the main thing I want to know if it really sounds as likely as I think or I'm just... overthinking it, I guess. Or if there could be something else. Right now, I don't know how to go about a diagnosis nor would I have the money and/or resources, but this thing is bothering me and I want to know if I have a point to even consider it until further action.

I'm an adult, I'm not that little girl anymore and it's not fair to make it as if it's a valid argument for anything ("Oh remember you were acting like a child when you were a child?" basically). title: I’ve known something is medically wrong with me for my entire life but I’ve never received a diagnosis.
selftext:
I’m a 23 year old female and I feel like my body is deteriorating. This is going to be a very long post but please stay with me here (especially if you’re an endocrinologist) - I’m begging to be pointed in the right direction. 

I’ve had anxiety, depression and ADHD for my entire life. Outside of that I’ve never been diagnosed with any serious medical conditions (I do have very low vitamin D if this counts - last test was 19ng/mL). I eat a well balanced and nutrient dense diet. I don’t lift or run much anymore due to such bad joint pain, but I work in hospitality so I’m on my feet all day, everyday and when I’m not at work I like to go for walks or hikes. I take 300mg of Wellbutrin daily and 50,000 IU’s of Vitamin D2 weekly.

Now here are the symptoms I have developed in the last 1-2 years:

- Hair is thinning & falling out (chunks of hair when I brush) - I’m developing a lot of hair loss in the front of my head, patches are starting. Started having a super dry scalp and dandrufff too.
- Nails consistently break no matter what I do 
- Severe inflammatory acne on lower half of face - never EVER have had acne before in my entire life, I’ve been blessed until now
- Joint pain all the time - neck/back/knees/legs - have to stretch my whole body before I can even walk around after waking up
- Menstrual cycle - consistently comes every month but with very heavy bleeding, blood clots, severe cramps, nausea, headaches, mood swings. Weird because usually it’ll be extreme for 2 days then stop for a day, then moderate for 1-2 days then stop altogether, spotting between periods for the first time ever (this has all existed since I got my period at age 10, only was better when I was on the pill which I can’t go back on)
- I’m tired all the time and my body hurts ALL the time. I work 40-45 hours a week and I HAVE to sleep the majority of my 2 days off in order to have enough energy to go back to work
- I’m FREEZING all the time (like, in weather anything under 60 degrees) when I used to sweat ALL the time

I should mention, if relevant, that I did suffer from pelvic pain (vulvodynia) from the age of 15 (maybe younger) to 20. Pelvic pain specialist said it was an inflammation based condition, and fully resolved the problem by taking me off of my hormonal birth control. Then I had an IUD from age 20 to 22. I didn’t have any side effects, but I had it taken out 2 years ago.

At 21, I woke up one morning with severe stabbing pain from the top of my neck to the lower part of my spine. I went to the hospital, they gave me no diagnosis but referred me to a rheumatologist and an infectious disease specialist. ID doc found nothing and rheumatologist said I had some kind of inflammatory arthritis. Went on Prednisone, had a reaction, stopped the medication, lived with the pain, eventually it went away. But I’ve had general neck and back pain for as long as I can remember so I just suffered through it. I also have moderate constant pain in both of my knees, they hurt ALL THE TIME.

At 18, I saw an endocrinologist due to an extensive family history of thyroid disorders. My antibodies were relatively high and other thyroid levels slightly off. Ultrasound showed slight abnormalities. No diagnosis or concern from the doctor. TPO 21, thyroglobulin antibody 1.9, T4 1.24, T3 167, TSH 0.99. Also said I have a large goiter. 

I’ve seen two different endocrinologists this year. First one said I probably have Hashimoto’s based on my symptoms. She retested my antibodies and they were normal, as were all thyroid levels. She also put me back on vitamin D because it was dangerously low. She said the chance of Hashimoto’s then was “less likely” and to “not worry” but offered no ideas for resolving my symptoms. 

Relevant bloodwork from Jan 2024: TSH 0.88, T4 1.29, testosterone serum 10, free testosterone 1.4%, free testosterone 1.4, thyroglobulin antibody <1.0, TPO 14. Estradiol was 30.7 during ovulation.

I’ve been told that the rest of my bloodwork shows I’m “very healthy” (of course, I don’t feel this way at all). No iron deficiency. I also feel like I could have PCOS but I’m not sure.

Second doctor was more convinced I have Hashimoto’s and told me to take Selenium and try a gluten-free and dairy-free diet, which I’ve been doing for two weeks. I may have a bit more energy but haven’t noticed any significant symptoms yet. Neither doctor performed an ultrasound (should they have?) - she said she couldn’t even tell what the abnormalities on the previous ultrasound were. Also said I have a large goiter but not to worry about that - physics exam was fine. I’ve been to multiple OBGYN’s, they offer no solution but to get another IUD. I don’t want to do that - I want to figure out what’s wrong with me and not let it cover my symptoms.

I really need help. I need to be pointed in the right direction, because I’m not sure where to go from here. I’m 23 years old and becoming extremely insecure about my hair, acne and the fact that normal workouts are too painful. But besides that, I really just want to feel better overall - mentally & physically. I want to be able to lift again, to feel confident and to feel healthy. I’ve dealt with these symptoms for the last year or two but something has ALWAYS felt off and I don’t want to live like this anymore. Thanks in advance.

title: How could this be happening at 41!!?!
selftext:
Early this morning (1:15am-ish) I heard the car start, and the garage door open. I called my husband’s cell to find out where he was going, and he said to Jacksonville, which is 45 minutes away. I asked him why he was going to Jacksonville, and he said, “I have always wanted to see Jacksonville.”

I gently reminded him of the time of night, and that maybe we can go together to see the city. He was amiable to the suggestion. He said he’d turn around at the nearest light and come home.  He arrives home twenty minutes later.. I asked him why it took so long to come, and he said he wanted to visit the local children’s park, this is at 1:40am.

He has chronic insomnia, which the physicians cannot get to the root cause. *see list below of what they have prescribed* 

He also has PTSD and often shouts out in his sleep screaming ‘help,’ or ‘look! Look! Look!.’ 

There are times I find him sitting at the edge of the bed, and staring out the window during civil twilight. 

And the very strange thing is that he is 41 years old. I want to cry, because he’s so young and the behavior doesn’t match. I’m exhausted with worrying about him….

Medication list :

5-HTP - 200MG QHS

Alprazolam ER - 2MG QHS

Ambien - 10MG QHS

Dozepin - 10MG QHS

Keppra - 500 BID for seizure control

Lamotrigine - 150MGBID

Lisinopril - 10MG BID

Midazolam - 5MG - 10MG given via nasal as a rescue medication 

Magnesium - 420MG as chelated Glycinate QHS

Melatonin - 10MG QHS

Metformin - 500 MG BID

Oxycodone - 10/325 TID (except 3 hrs before bedtime) 

Tizanidine 10MG TID

—————Discontinued —————

Amitriptyline - D/C d/t an increase in blood sugar 

Halcion - D/C d/t short half-life

Lunesta - D/C d/t prolonged metallic taste

Trazodone - D/C d/t Bradycardia

title: Growing pains that never went away and plethora of other symptoms
selftext:
I'm AFAB in my late 20s. I've had multiple weird and painful symptoms since a young age. As a kid and teen, the pains i had in my joints, lower back, knees, etc always got chalked off as growing pains. Im past 25 years old now and still in so much pain. It prevents me from having a normal life, prevents me from sleeping also. My feet, knees, hips, lower back, shoulders, and neck hurt the most.     
 I stretch, walk daily, exercise, eat my vegetables, fruits and proteins, drink water, etc. I've had blood tests ran and everything is normal according to my family doctor. She doesnt know why someone "so young" would be in this kind of pain.      
I also get heart palpitations, chest pains, dizzy, lightheaded (especially when standing up from a laid down or sitting position), I'm chronically tired and fatigued, I honestly dont remember the last time i had a normal healthy looking bowel movement, I have a hyperactive bladder, sometimes my hands will tremble and itll feel like my legs are turning into jello, i have stomach pains when hungry and when I eat (to the point im in a fetus position and crying sometimes), my hips crack and pop when i walk and its very painful, and i can go on honestly. 

My doctor says its anxiety, my psychiatrist says its physical. Ive been in various mental health therapies since 2018. I was diagnosed with ADHD and Borderline personality disorder last year and am now taking 20mg vyvanse daily. Please help me, the next time i see my family doctor i want to arrive with ideas of things she can look for/into.

Happens for maybe 10-20 seconds then stops.

Any ideas?

title: Sexual harassment by therapist. Crossed ethical boundaries.
selftext:
42 year old Hispanic/White female. 5’2 118lbs. No drugs. No alcohol. 

Anxiety Disorder 
Ativan as needed 

I walked out during my last therapy session because I had enough of my therapist making sexually inappropriate comments towards me. I have body dysmorphia and he would tell me things like, I don’t know why you think you’re so ugly. I think you’re hot. You’re sexy. 

There were many times he’d interrupt me when I’d be talking saying things like, I like your hands, I like your shirt. You have great legs. 

I tried to ignore these comments but I’d finally had enough. I calmly confronted him and told him he was making me uncomfortable. He then lost it and started yelling at me. He told me I wanted him to say these things to me and I’m the problem because I just hate all men. This is simply not true as I’m married and love my husband. 

As he was yelling at me I froze, like I was back in trauma defense mode. I was shaking but I stood up and just walked out not saying anything. He asked me where I was going and I calmly said, I think I need a new therapist. 

He is a PhD and owns the practice. My son and I see the nurse practitioner there for our medication. I called yesterday to schedule an appointment for my son for his ADD with the nurse practitioner and was told we could no longer be seen there. 

My husband told me to report him to the state board but I’m scared. I really don’t want to go over all my trauma and reasons for seeing him with someone from the board that I don’t know. I also never want to see him again. 

Most of all I’ve been traumatized by this. I trusted this professional and now I’m scared to find someone else because of what happened. I really need to be in therapy for ptsd and body dysmorphia. I don’t know what to do.

title: Can repeated self harm to the same area create medical issues years later after stopping?
selftext:
I(25F) have autism and ADHD. They did not get diagnosed and treated until I was 18, turning 19. From age 13 to 20, I repeatedly and intensely punched my upper right thigh(knee to hip, sometimes waist) to the point where the entire thing would be purple. I played two sports and constantly trained for them in the off seasons, so I always blamed it on diving for volleyballs and getting hit by tennis balls. Although there were sometimes more bruises than other times, there was rarely a time where there wasn’t a bruise.

This also means that while I was hitting and bruising my leg in the same area, I was training and doing intense exercises that mainly involved my legs, including heavy weight leg exercises(my thigh muscles at the time were very large for a teenage girl to the point where finding pants that fit correctly became an issue, and my body fat percentage was always around 18. I was very strong for my size, and I punched myself like I meant it every time. 

The self harm waned quickly when I went to college and completely when I started the right SSRI and neuro stimulant(right before I turned 20). These meds were life changing for me when used in conjunction of therapy and the freedom to develop a solid sense of self. 

However, now at 25 my leg keeps feeling numb and my hip makes a cracking sound when I move it. Menstrual cramps especially create a pain that radiates down my legs and it’s concerning to me. I also have a few rather large, rock hard lymph nodes around my body, in which a few exceed a centimeter. 


I also stopped exercising as intensely, but would still run a total of about 20 miles a week up until I was 22, which was when COVID hit, and I also had surgery on my shoulder from tearing a muscle. Recovery took much longer than expected. Then, I started having seizures and was scared to run by myself. Now I typically just do cardio on a indoor cycling bike four times a week.

Just to be clear I am in NO danger of harming myself. I have a much healthier relationship with my own body and have much more control over myself, as well as having the skills to set boundaries with people that don’t respect me and my limits. 

(For background, the self harming tendencies were a response to immediate frustration and distress when I couldn’t process my emotions or felt mad at myself, and they started when I was a baby/toddler, but never got past scratching my own skin with my fingernails until puberty hit. All of the pressures of teenage life were difficult, but I was an easy target for being harassed. My own, narcissistic, conservative, and very religious father also made things worse as he would scream at me any time I had a “meltdown” and tell me that I was stupid and would only fail in life. He also would yell at me any time I wore makeup or clothing that was remotely tight. He would poke at me until I broke down, and he threw a fit when I went to college.  

I am now able to navigate that relationship without it causing me much distress.

For me, autism also does not present in decreased empathy, but rather hypersensitivity while still not picking up on social cues. Concrete thinking and feeling emotions intensely are my biggest, most obvious symptoms, along with needing routines and having “special interests.”

I was not diagnosed until later in life because I was very controlled, intelligent, and high achieving. I graduated high school in the top 10% of my class and made it through college with a 3.4 in a double major of economics and math. Because I was very nurturing as well and could connect to other people, I think the obvious symptoms were brushed off as being quirky. The only reason I was evaluated was because I was on a run with a friend and mistakenly stepped in front of a car, causing me to get hit and landed on my head on the concrete after flying 8 feet. At my follow up appointment with the neurologist, he said he wanted to look into why I didn’t see the car despite looking both ways, especially after I described how I experienced it unfolding). 

I manage all of my symptoms very well at this point in my life, so if there is something that you think will make me panic or cause me to fixate, please do not hold it back. I prefer to know the truth of any possibility just as I think anyone else would. Please don’t think as though you have to tiptoe around anything.

title: How could this be happening at 41!!?!
selftext:
Early this morning (1:15am-ish) I heard the car start, and the garage door open. I called my husband’s cell to find out where he was going, and he said to Jacksonville, which is 45 minutes away. I asked him why he was going to Jacksonville, and he said, “I have always wanted to see Jacksonville.”

I gently reminded him of the time of night, and that maybe we can go together to see the city. He was amiable to the suggestion. He said he’d turn around at the nearest light and come home.  He arrives home twenty minutes later.. I asked him why it took so long to come, and he said he wanted to visit the local children’s park, this is at 1:40am.

He has chronic insomnia, which the physicians cannot get to the root cause. *see list below of what they have prescribed* 

He also has PTSD and often shouts out in his sleep screaming ‘help,’ or ‘look! Look! Look!.’ 

There are times I find him sitting at the edge of the bed, and staring out the window during civil twilight. 

And the very strange thing is that he is 41 years old. I want to cry, because he’s so young and the behavior doesn’t match. I’m exhausted with worrying about him….

5-HTP - 200MG QHS

Alprazolam ER - 2MG QHS

Keppra - 500 BID for seizure control

title: Please help. Am I making cancer recovery difficult eating a Keto diet?
selftext:
Background:

Woman, 50-60yrs old (anonymity due to abusive ex)

For the past 1.5 yrs, I've been battling a resurgence of cervical cancer that I had 20 yrs ago.

As a result of a left hemispheric stroke over a dozen years ago, the entire right side of my body has seizures. I was on the 3600 mg/day and still had seizures. 

That was until my research lead me to discover that the keto diet was actually created as a treatment for epilepsy. I cut out sugar and carbs and the seizures were cut in half almost instantaneously.

I also have active MRSA cysts due to a SSI three years ago during a double mastectomy with reconstruction.

Current:

I had the third surgery for cervical cancer almost two weeks ago, and aside from the sheer exhaustion of recovering, I've been fairly pain and infection free. Nice!

However, the ongoing sheer exhaustion is crippling. 

I've been maintaining a strict keto diet throughout recovery as 1) seizures + exhaustion = misery and 2) I don't have the required level of activity needed to burn calories. 

I am very self conscious of the weight I gained after the December surgery due to the inactivity caused by pain. Plus the hormonal changes that have changed my metabolism.

I'm eating nearly nothing, a chicken breast and a couple handfuls of almonds, per day. Normally that would be fine however, now, I'm craving carbs. So I'll have a piece of toast with lots of butter and peanut butter to get my fats in.

But I'm ***still*** craving carbs. If I have more carbs, it will trigger seizures and seizures are exhausting and painful. Imagine charlie horses but in every muscle all of the time.

But I have this feeling like I'm not going to regain my strength if I don't eat more. I also don't have the mental wherewithal to properly research or process the information.As s single mama of several SN kiddos, I don't have the luxury of staying in bed either.

What diet advice, how do it eat, to get me back to normalish?

title: Unsure what to do now.
selftext:
I have seen several doctors and have had several ER trips, but am still awaiting a diagnosis. Posting here to see if anyone has any advice. I apologize for the length, I just want to be thorough. 

I am a 23 year old female, 5'6" and about 125lbs. The only medication I take is birth control pills and I also have a copper IUD that was implanted almost 18 months ago.  My personal medical history: postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, CPTSD, and ADHD. Family history of ventricular fibrillation (paternal grandmother), hypertension (paternal grandparents, father), prostate cancer (paternal grandfather), and breast cancer (maternal great grandmother, maternal aunt, mother  was dx w/ cancer at 34yo). 

In August, I started experiencing the following symptoms:
- Light vaginal bleeding that lasted weeks
- Feeling full quickly while eating
- Urinary urgency
- Dull abdominal pain in my lower belly
I saw my gynecologist in early August to see if something was wrong with my IUD. She did a pelvic exam but didn't find anything concerning, my IUD strings were in place. She told me to stop my birth control for a week and come back the next week. 

I did as instructed, but by my second appointment the bleeding had stopped. I was now having severe, sharp lower left abdominal pain as well as the dull pain in the center of my lower abdomen. The pain would make me double over or would wake me up. She ordered a transvaginal ultrasound and told me to follow up with my PCP to rule out a possible GI issue.

I saw my PCP a week later and was referred to gastroenterology pending the results of my ultrasound.

I had my ultrasound done on August 28th. By this point, since early August, I had lost a total of 10 pounds. The ultrasound was very painful and several hours afterward I began having intense abdominal pain and heavy vaginal bleeding. I went to the ER on August 29th. 

The ER docs were immediately concerned for ovarian cancer given my symptoms and family history. I was now also experiencing daily nausea/vomiting. They did a lot of blood work, which all came back normal, and a CT scan of my abdomen. My ultrasound results were not yet available.

CT showed a "moderately large" 4.5 centimeter mass on my left ovary. The ER docs said they couldn't determine for sure if it was fluid filled or solid, and told me to see gynecology immediately, if not a gynecological oncologist.

The ultrasound results came in a couple days later and confirmed the mass on my ovary, but was measuring a full centimeter smaller than was was recorded on CT. According to the ultrasound it looked like a simple fluid filled cyst. It was still recommended that I seen gyn onc, so I made an appointment.

I saw a wonderful, incredibly kind world-renowned gynecological oncologist on September 10th. She was very thorough and took me seriously. My CA125 came back very normal, as did all other labs including vitamin D. Negative for pregnancy and UTI. She personally reviewed my images and said it was just a simple cyst, but we could discuss surgery if it gets bigger. She ordered an MRI and another ultrasound.

I felt reassured that it wasn't cancer at this point, but still concerned that I didn't have answers. I planned on getting that imaging done soon.

Well, no need for that. On September 14th, I was pushing around some heavy stuff at work when I had a sudden sharp pain in my left side that made me fall to my knees. I started bleeding very heavily again. I tried to tough it out for as long as I could but once I started vomiting and I developed a fever 24 hours later, I went back to the ER. 

I had another ultrasound which showed no evidence of torsion. The cyst on my left ovary was gone and I now had a large volume of unidentified free fluid in my abdomen with blood components, as well as two new, smaller cysts on my right ovary. My left cyst had obviously ruptured.

I was sent home after a few hours, and although I was in a lot of pain and I was super bloated, I felt even more reassured since cysts are very common and ruptured cysts aren't abnormal or necessarily concerning either. I assumed that once my body absorbed the blood and fluid from the cyst I'd feel a lot better. 

Nope. 

In the 6 weeks since my cyst ruptured, my symptoms did start to resolve but then come back with a vengeance. Still experiencing all of the same symptoms, except now I'm gaining weight. I dropped down to about 115 and now I'm back to 125 without any changes in diet. It seems that the weight is all in my belly, which is hard and bloated. My legs and arms seem thinner. I am now very constipated. I cannot have a bowel movement without taking at least 6 doses of miralax, and even then it's not much. I have so much urgency to urinate that I have wet myself many times while trying to make it to the restroom. My fatigue is so bad that I fall asleep at work regularly, even though I am sleeping all the time and have a high adrenaline, fast paced job (I work in the emergency room and in surgery). I still have irregular bleeding that lasts for weeks. 

My MRI has been scheduled and then cancelled and rescheduled several times, but I'm trying to get that done as soon as possible. My oncologist wants to wait to see me until after the imaging is done.

Also, not sure if it's related, but I did have a TIA while at work on October 12th, which landed me back in the ER. That was my first and only one. I did not have a stroke, that was ruled out. During this ER visit, they did a bunch more blood work. All was normal aside from my potassium (which was a tiny bit low) and also I had very high lymphocytes. My lymphocyte numbers more than quintupled in four weeks. They were on the low end of normal in September and then very high in October.

I tried getting an appointment with my PCP, gynecologist, and GI but they are all booked up for months. 

I'm really concerned and don't know where to go or what to do from here besides just wait for it to get worse. I have no idea what's wrong with me. 

Any advice at all would be really appreciated.

title: What were the people in my head?
selftext:
I tried to ask this over on the AskPsychology sub reddit, but something about this post kept flagging their automod and I couldn't figure out what it is. 

23F, 195lbs, 5'2, White 

Disclaimer: I do not have DID, I do not have any amnesia, and my childhood was normal and happy. 

When I was in my early teens, I developed some mental health issues. I would eventually be diagnosed with ADHD, OCD, MDD, GAD, and PMDD. I wasn't diagnosed until my late teens/early adulthood because I actively hid these struggles from others until I was no longer able to. 

During this time of hiding, I (involuntarily) developed things that I called "entities". They were like...personifications of my emotions, almost. They all had specific jobs and goals and roles in the little inner world that I made for myself, and it all had to do with living life out in the "real" world. 

Keep in mind, I never switched with thwsw entities, I never had memory loss, I never had the sense that someone else was controlling my body. In addition, I also didn't physically hear any of their voices. It was the same as the voice you are using to read this post right now. It was mine, but...it wasn't? 

I didn't control what they did or said. They just sorta existed, and I would watch them work shit out whenever the "outside" life got bad. And I could interact with them, and they all knew what they were and what I was, but...idk. 

Now that I've been diagnosed and had medicine for a while, they're gone. Or at least, I can't reach them. I used to feel so emotionally broken down that I would feel myself sorts "split" and that's when these entities would become more prominent, but things have been really good for a while now so I have no access to them. 

I sorta miss them. I don't know what they were, though. Any and all insight is welcome. If you have questions, I'll answer them in the comments.

6'2"
85kg
White
UK
PMHx: Depression, ADHD, ?Autism.

deficient in B12 and got diagnosed with adhd (not
currently medicated). Could it have been either of these all along?

title: I’m scared I’m becoming a psychopath
selftext:
Growing up, I was never a normal kid. I had really strong signs of autism starting around age 4. I didn’t know many words, and I often made my own words up for things. My parents never diagnosed me, but instead they decided to change my diet to a completely gluten-free diet. That started at around 8 years old. Believe it or not, it helped tremendously, which makes me think now that I just have super bad ADHD and eating wheat makes it even worse. I had really bad anger issues as a kid, but it wasn’t so much harmful as it was stupid. I tried to be the best at everything, and if I wasn’t, I’d get pissed off. This seemed to end around high school. I didn’t care as much about being the best, but more about just making it through high school. I had few friends, but the friends I had are still my friends to this day. I didn’t care about being popular, and I often hated the kids that were. So now that I’ve given a little bit of a background, I will go into detail about why I feel like I’m becoming a psychopath

I’m 21 now, but life outside of high school has absolutely destroyed me. I was in a 2 year toxic relationship that ended in disaster. She didn’t cheat on me or anything, but she slept with a guy pretty much right after we broke up, and told me all about how he was a way better person than I was, and that she’d do everything for him that she never did for me. It pissed me off so much, this was the first time I ever scared myself. I had continuous panic attacks for at least 3 days. I had begun smoking weed about a year ago to this day, right after she moved really far away for college. I was still in the relationship when I started. I noticed that when I started smoking, my anxiety went away, and so did any of my compassion for my ex. I had confidence in myself, and I guess I just felt like I really didn’t need her anymore. I’m gonna give myself a little grace, because she was definitely not the right girl for me. But it felt like the only way I could love is if I was super anxious. It’s like I couldn’t love just to love. When I started smoking weed, it made me ignore my ex more than usual. It’s like I really didn’t want as much to do with her, because I was happy with myself. This went on to the point where I just got so tired of her whining about it that I broke up with her. I quit weed after I broke up with her and I was off of it for a good 2 months. We had taken a break at that point, since I ended up moving far away, but once I moved back, we got back together for about a month, since she was back home for the summer. I broke up with her again and she decided to sleep with someone else and it completely changed how I felt. I could tell it was happening, since I was still talking to her at that point. I was spamming her like crazy trying to get an answer out of her. I’d call her until she answered and I wouldn’t give it up. I started smoking weed again because I could see it coming, but this time it didn’t help so much with the anxiety. I got so upset at her, that I went to the lengths of emailing her since that was the only thing I wasn’t blocked on. I told her stuff like “I never loved you, jokes on you, I cheated the whole time” when in reality I never cheated. I just wanted to go out of the relationship feeling like I didn’t lose anything, and that she was the one who was truly hurting.

This was the first time I scared myself. I drove hours to see her pretty much every weekend, but it always upset me so much that she didn’t try to save my cars or gas by getting a license and driving to me instead. (she was 19 before she even started driving, literally a year into the relationship) by the time we broke up for good, she had driven a little bit, but I was pretty much still always the one to drive to her. Which is why it pissed me off so much when she drove 2 hours to sleep with a guy. This developed such an anxiety and anger in me that I felt like I had to say nasty things to her. I felt so disowned in that moment. I felt like I needed control.

I stopped emailing her about 2 days after what happened. But I smoked way too much weed for a solid 4 months. It would get to the point where the high was wearing off and I was no longer enjoying it. So I decided to quit. The first time I tried quitting, I lasted 2 weeks and went right back to it. Now I am 3 weeks sober, and I plan on staying like that. I still hate my ex to this day, but I don’t feel the need to talk to her or anything. So it’s not like I can’t let things go necessarily, but it’s like I wanted control over the situation so badly that I went to crazy lengths to try and stop her from sleeping with that guy. I don’t have thoughts of murder or anything, but at one point I was wishing death on her, because I literally couldn’t control my emotions. I even threatened to kill myself if she hadn’t given me an answer on whether she was sleeping with that guy or not (I wasn’t actually going to, which makes it scarier) my emotions had gotten so out of hand, but for only about 2 days. 

Since I’ve quit weed, I’ve become more and more scared that I’m becoming a psychopath. I’m constantly doing research to find out if I’m a psychopath or not. I cried as a kid, but I haven’t cried much lately. I feel like I can still feel sadness, but it’s just complicated. I feel like I have to pressure myself to cry or I’m a psychopath. I have weird intrusive thoughts that drive me crazy. Thoughts that I don’t want. I’ll be imagining someone picking on me, and beating them up or threatening to kill them, but I feel like my brain prevents me from actually visualizing it. These episodes have been happening since I quit weed, and they tend to last 10-15 minutes. I calm myself down and usually think about the right way to handle the imaginary situation, but I still scare myself so much. I want these thoughts to end. I don’t wanna be like this forever. I get super anxious when this happens and my heart races, so I feel like the whole death threat thing just comes from me being small, knowing I can’t win a fight unless the person is similar in size to me, so I see it more as self defense than anything. But it’s still so confusing because maybe it isn’t a self defense thing?? Maybe I’m actually a psychopath?? Or am I just crazy? Or maybe I’m a narcissist with really bad trust issues?? 

I swear if I find out I’m a psychopath, I will literally kill myself. I could maybe live with being a narcissist, but I feel like all purpose in my life would be robbed from me. I’m in such an awful mental state right now and I don’t know if I’ll ever get better again…
