We had taken a break at that point, since I ended up moving far away, but once I moved back, we got back together for about a month, since she was back home for the summer. I broke up with her again and she decided to sleep with someone else and it completely changed how I felt. I could tell it was happening, since I was still talking to her at that point. I was spamming her like crazy trying to get an answer out of her. I’d call her until she answered and I wouldn’t give it up. I started smoking weed again because I could see it coming, but this time it didn’t help so much with the anxiety. I got so upset at her, that I went to the lengths of emailing her since that was the only thing I wasn’t blocked on. I told her stuff like “I never loved you, jokes on you, I cheated the whole time” when in reality I never cheated. I just wanted to go out of the relationship feeling like I didn’t lose anything, and that she was the one who was truly hurting.

title: I think this is more serious than ADHD
selftext:
Age: 26

Sex: Male

Height: 6'2"

Weight: 218

Race: Caucasian

Duration of complain: 9 Months

Location (Geographic and on body): Cognitive, Mid/Right back, lower neck, between shoulders

Any existing relevant medical issues (if any): ADHD, anxiety

Current medications (if any): Adderall (Generic)



I'll try to keep this short. This all started in January as a complaint to my PCP regarding sleep problems. I went for a sleep study, no sleep problems. The primary issues are all very similar to ADHD-PI:


**Unable to Focus**: If I'm being talked to about something, I wind up immediately tuning that person out and trying to stay awake


**Memory**: I have a very difficult time remembering things and all too frequently forget words that I need mid sentence. I have recently been forgetting what I'm talking about mid sentence with coworkers (very embarrassing) as if I walked off a cliff mid sentence


**Severe Lack of Motivation**: I can no longer bring myself to do the most basic or important tasks. I'm putting things off more frequently than ever. I miss putting things off because I didn't want to do them, now it's because I physically "CAN'T".



Also:


**Vision**: My vision seems to be closing in (tunnel vision) and I have more frequent eye floaters than normal. This scares the living hell out of me as I've always been very sharp and aware of my surroundings. Also makes me worry about things like Glaucoma.


**Absent Minded**: And that is absolutely literal. Yesterday, I sat at my desk clicking in and out of browser windows for at least an hour without really knowing what I was doing. I'm almost done with this post and I'm already head in the clouds, not really remembering entirely what I've already said. 


**Feel Drunk/High/Not There**: I'm moving through the world in a way that doesn't feel real. It may have something to do with the vision. I wouldn't consider it depersonalization, but I feel as if it could be eventually if this isn't fixed.




The diagnosis of ADHD-PI came in February as I had finished up an IT certification and noticed it was very difficult. My stories from childhood were enough alone for the diagnosis and I can't say that I don't have a level of ADHD, but this feels neurological. The Adderall helps with the symptoms I'm experiencing for the most part, but at times I feel like I'm just high at work.



Also worthy of noting is that the back/neck pain is much more recent than when the issues all started. It isn't debilitating pain, but it only makes me think there is a pinched nerve causing my problems.



Any advice is greatly appreciated. I want to figure this out as 'cheap' as possible as I already have racked up debt trying to figure this out.

title: Possible reasons for low magnesium despite healthy diet?
selftext:
ISSUE
- Lifelong high need/demand for Magnesium despite healthy diet
- I start having twitchy muscles if I’m a couple hours late in taking my Mg supplement. Literally wakes me up in the night. 
- Noticeable hair loss, anxiety, mental fatigue, CONSTANT hunger, etc if I stop the Mg supplement for ≥1 week.

1) Is this something to be concerned about? Is this a possible symptom of an underlying condition or deficiency? If so, what type of doctor or tests would be appropriate? 

2) Is it possible for such extreme high demand or poor absorption of Mg to be a normal genetic variance? 

——————

5”7” , 127-132 lbs 

170 cm , 57-60 kg
- physically active 3-5 x week (yoga, hiking, running, calisthenics)

	* I’ve read that chronic stimulant use can deplete electrolyte levels (is this true?), but all my cravings existed before my ADHD Dx and Rx.

- Omnivore, but I try to avoid beef due to (undiagnosed) arthritis flare ups in R knee and ankle
- Little to no processed food, gluten, or sugar.
- Dairy free since 2016
- 3-10 servings fruit &amp;amp; veg daily
- I don’t count calories, but generally am known for having a very hearty appetite/ high metabolism

Allergies 
- Casein protein (Dairy)
- Penicillin
- Mild gluten intolerance 

History

- I run very VERY cold. If I’m comfortable, then everyone else is sweating. Mg supplements don’t seem to affect this.


For my entire life I’ve had almost constant cravings for dark greens, ≥ 75% dark chocolate, and sweet potatoes. It’s a bit the family joke, since I eat them in almost every meal. I never saw an issue with it since they’re healthy for you.

It was LIFECHANGING. 

All emotional turmoil and the constant hunger immediately stopped within 48hrs, my hair has started to grow back, weight went back down to normal, etc. Also noticed that any residual soreness on my fracture lines disappeared after a week or so.

Did some research and discovered all my favorite foods/cravings are for things high in Mg and realized this has been a lifelong thing... which is how i ended up here.
